memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All the Israelite men and women who were willing brought to the Lord freewill offerings for all the work the Lord through Moses had commanded them to do." - Exod 35:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse gathers the whole scene into one sentence, and the word "freewill" sits at its heart.

Nobody was audited. No amounts were announced. The word "willing" or "willingly" appears again and again through this chapter — it is the theme God wants us to notice.

Compare this with what happened at the calf. There, Aaron told them to hand over their gold, and they did it under the pressure of a crowd. Here, they give because their hearts moved them. The same act, done from a completely different source.

God has always cared about the source, not just the substance. Israel would later be rebuked for offerings given while their hearts were far away (Isa 29:13). Ananias and Sapphira gave generously and were condemned, because the giving was theatre (Acts 5:1-4).

This should relieve us and search us at the same time. Relieve, because God is not looking for a performance we cannot sustain. Search, because He sees what is underneath what we do.

The gospel makes willing giving possible. We give because we have received — freely you have received, freely give (Matt 10:8). Christ gave Himself for us, and generosity is simply the natural shape of a heart that has grasped it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your giving free, or driven by pressure and appearance?
2. What would change if no one ever knew what you gave?
3. How has Christ's generosity toward you shaped your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make my giving free and glad. I have received so much from You — let it flow outward. Amen.
